name: academy-award-best-picture

description.en: Every film that has won the Academy Award for Best Picture, from Wings at the 1st ceremony (1929) to One Battle After Another at the 98th (15 March 2026), the latest as of 4 October 2026: 98 cards, one per ceremony. Front: the ceremony's number and the year it was held, e.g. "Best Picture at the 71st Academy Awards (1999)"; back: the film, in Swedish under its Swedish title where it has one. Taken from Wikidata and checked against the Academy's ceremony pages and the English and Swedish Wikipedia. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
description.sv: Varje film som har vunnit Oscar för bästa film, från Vingarna vid den 1:a galan (1929) till One Battle After Another vid den 98:e (15 mars 2026), den senaste per den 4 oktober 2026: 98 kort, ett per gala. Framsida: galans nummer och året den hölls, t.ex. ”Bästa film vid den 71:a Oscarsgalan (1999)”; baksida: filmen, på svenska under sin svenska titel där den har en. Uppgifterna är hämtade från Wikidata och kontrollerade mot den amerikanska filmakademiens webbsidor om galorna och mot engelska och svenska Wikipedia. Inte knuten till eller godkänd av Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

1. Wikidata (query 1): every non-deprecated P166 (award received) statement whose value is Academy Award for Best Picture (Q102427), with its P585 (point in time) and P805 (statement is subject of: the ceremony) qualifiers, the ceremony's English label and its own P585 date, and the English and Swedish labels of the item, was fetched as CSV from the Wikidata Query Service. Wikidata records the award on the films and also on their producers (people), so the result holds 240 rows. Every ceremony from the 1st Academy Awards to the 98th appears; one row without a ceremony, on the directing duo "Daniels" (Q30122828, not a film, with a P585 of 2022), was not used. Query 2 restricted the statements to items that are instances of film or of a subclass of film (P31/P279* Q11424) and have a P805 ceremony, and fetched every English, Swedish and multilingual (mul) label and alias: exactly one film for each of the 98 ceremonies, no ceremony with two. The front's year is the year of the ceremony item's P585 (the day the ceremony was held), not the P585 qualifier of the award statement, which on some films holds only the ceremony year (year precision, shown by the Query Service as 1 January; e.g. Mrs. Miniver, Marty, Chariots of Fire) and on All Quiet on the Western Front two values (1930 at year precision and November 1930 at month precision).

2. The Academy's own record (query 4): the ceremony page on oscars.org for every year from 1929 to 2026 was read with WebFetch (a tool that fetches a page, converts it to text and answers a question about it; curl from the research environment got HTTP 403 from oscars.org, so the pages were not saved). For each page the tool was asked to quote the heading, the date the ceremony was held, the name of the top film category and the winning film. The pages are addressed by year: the address year is the year the ceremony was held, except that the pages of the 3rd, 4th and 5th ceremonies (held on 5 November 1930, 10 November 1931 and 18 November 1932) are at 1931, 1932 and 1933 and say so in their headings ("The 3rd Academy Awards | 1931"); cmp2.py compared the date and the winning film of every reading with Wikidata (the ceremony item's P585; the film's English labels and aliases, ignoring case) and found no disagreement. The 98th ceremony's page says it was held on Sunday, March 15, 2026, and gives "One Battle after Another" as Best Picture; the 2027 page says "No ceremony in 2027." A web search on the day ("98th Academy Awards Best Picture winner March 2026") returned news reports of the 98th ceremony on March 15, 2026 with One Battle After Another as Best Picture. The Academy's searchable Awards Database (awardsdatabase.oscars.org) answered WebFetch with a "Browser Unsupported" page and was not used.

3. English Wikipedia (query 5): the article "Academy Award for Best Picture" was fetched with its revision id through the MediaWiki API, and wp.py took from each decade table the first (gold, bold) row after each ceremony number "(1st)" … "(98th)". It names the same film as Wikidata for all 98 ceremonies. Its section "Category name changes" gives the award's names: Outstanding Picture (1st–2nd ceremonies), Outstanding Production (3rd–13th), Outstanding Motion Picture (14th–16th), Best Motion Picture (17th–34th) and Best Picture since the 35th; the category names on the oscars.org pages agree.

4. Swedish titles (queries 5 and 6): the Swedish Wikipedia list "Oscar för bästa film" was fetched with its revision id, and wp.py took the bold winner of each ceremony (the row heading links "(1:a)" … "(98:e)" to "Oscarsgalan <year>", for 1930 "Oscarsgalan april 1930" and "Oscarsgalan november 1930"). svintro.py then fetched the opening sentences of the 98 Swedish articles these rows link to, with their revision ids and Wikidata items; every article is the Swedish article of the same Wikidata item as the card. The Swedish articles name a film by its Swedish title where it has one and give the original title in brackets ("Gudfadern (engelska: The Godfather) är …"). The Swedish title on each card is the Wikidata sv label (or the mul label where there is no sv label: Forrest Gump, Everything Everywhere All at Once), and agrees with the Swedish article, except in five cases where the card follows the Swedish article and its history (see quality control): Komedien om oss människor (11th), Tom Jones (36th), Patton – Pansargeneralen (43rd), French Connection – Lagens våldsamma män (44th) and CODA (94th). Svensk Filmdatabas (Svenska Filminstitutet), the reference for Swedish release titles, answered HTTP 403 to curl and to WebFetch from the research environment (query 7), so the Swedish titles rest on Wikidata and the Swedish Wikipedia alone; the web searches of query 7 were not used as evidence.

5. Cross-check: cmp1.py compared, ceremony by ceremony, the Wikidata film and its English and Swedish labels with the English and Swedish Wikipedia winners, and the year of the ceremony's P585 with the Swedish list's "Oscarsgalan <year>" link; cmp2.py compared the oscars.org readings with Wikidata (step 2). The film is the same in all four sources for all 98 ceremonies, and the years agree. The differences found are all in the form of titles (capitalisation, punctuation, short or full title, Swedish title) and are listed under quality control. make_dossier.py wrote this dossier from the saved files: the "says" texts of the Wikidata, English and Swedish Wikipedia evidence were generated from the parsed data, and those of oscars.org from the WebFetch answers recorded in oscars.txt; nothing in them was typed by hand. Corrections made after review (quality-control rounds 1 to 6) were applied by patch scripts from fresh fetches and are recorded there. The scripts are not published with the deck; the rules above are what they do.

6. Cards: front "Best Picture at the <ordinal> Academy Awards (<year>)" / "Bästa film vid den <ordinal> Oscarsgalan (<year>)", where the year is the year the ceremony was held (the films are from the year or years before). The ceremony number is on the front because two ceremonies were held in 1930 (the 2nd in April, the 3rd in November), so a year alone would be ambiguous. English ordinals 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 11th, 12th, 13th, 21st …; Swedish ordinals as in the library's other decks: a numeral, a colon and the last letter of the spelled-out ordinal: :a for numbers ending in 1 or 2 except 11 and 12, :e for all others (1:a, 2:a, 3:e, 11:e, 21:a, 22:a). Back: in English the Wikidata English label (or the mul label where the item has no English label: Forrest Gump, 67th; for the 11th ceremony the capitalisation "You Can't Take It with You" of oscars.org and the English Wikipedia, see step 7 and quality control), which is the English (for non-English films the international English) title; in Swedish the Swedish title, identical to the English one where the film was released in Sweden under its original title. Two back notes: on the 1st ceremony, that Sunrise won the separate Unique and Artistic Picture award (oscars.org's 1929 page; the English Wikipedia: the Academy dropped that award the following year), so that the front has one answer; on the 87th, the full title of Birdman. The fronts and notes are the compiler's own wording. Study direction front to back only: from a film back to the number of a ceremony is not a sensible question.

7. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the film holds P166 Q102427, that the ceremony item's P585 is in the year on the front, and, where the card's title is a Wikidata label or alias in that language (or mul), the English and Swedish titles. Where the card's title differs from every Wikidata label and alias (11th in English; 36th, 43rd and 44th in Swedish) the label check is left out and the difference is recorded under quality control. The checks cannot reach the P805 qualifier that ties a film to its ceremony; that rests on query 1 and the comparison in step 5 and is recorded in each card's evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).
selection: Every film that has won the Academy Award for Best Picture, one card for each of the 98 ceremonies from the 1st (16 May 1929) to the 98th (15 March 2026), the latest as of 4 October 2026: the 99th ceremony is to be held in 2027. The award has had several names (Outstanding Picture at the 1st and 2nd ceremonies, Outstanding Production, Outstanding Motion Picture, Best Motion Picture, and Best Picture since the 35th ceremony in 1963); it is the same award throughout and the deck calls it Best Picture. At the 1st ceremony the Academy also gave a separate award for Unique and Artistic Picture (to Sunrise), dropped the following year; it is not the Best Picture award and has no card, but a note on the 1st card names it. Left out: the nominees that did not win, the producers or studios who received the award, and every other Academy Award category.

licensing: The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of winners, the ceremony of each award and its date, and the English and Swedish titles all come from it, so the deck is CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The Academy's oscars.org pages (all rights reserved) and the English and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the Wikidata data gave, and no wording, table layout or selection was copied from them. Where the card's Swedish or English title follows the Swedish Wikipedia or the Academy rather than the Wikidata label (three Swedish titles, of the 36th, 43rd and 44th ceremonies, and one English capitalisation, of the 11th; two further Swedish titles, "Komedien om oss människor" (11th) and "CODA" (94th), differ from the Wikidata sv label but are a Wikidata sv alias and the mul label), what is taken is the title of a film, a fact that is not protected by copyright, not text or a selection. The selection is the complete set of Best Picture winners, which every list of the award shares because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from a list. The fronts and notes are the compiler's own wording. Academy Awards and Oscars are trademarks of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences; the deck uses the names only to identify the award and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Academy.

rounds.lens: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's ceremony, year and film against Wikidata, the Academy's ceremony pages and the English and Swedish Wikipedia; the Swedish titles against Wikidata sv labels and the Swedish Wikipedia articles and their histories.
rounds.scope: All 98 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.
rounds.summary: Wikidata, oscars.org and the English and Swedish Wikipedia name the same film for all 98 ceremonies, and the ceremony dates agree. The 98th ceremony was held on 15 March 2026 and is the latest as of 4 October 2026. The differences found are in the form of titles and in Wikidata's modelling; four label checks were left out where the card's title is better sourced than the Wikidata label, and each is recorded here. Svensk Filmdatabas could not be reached, so the Swedish titles rest on Wikidata and the Swedish Wikipedia.

findings.issue: Two ceremonies were held in 1930: the 2nd on 3 April and the 3rd on 5 November. A front keyed by the ceremony year alone would have two answers.
findings.resolution: Every front gives the ceremony number and the year it was held.

findings.issue: The 1st ceremony had two top film awards: Outstanding Picture (Wings), the award that became Best Picture, and Unique and Artistic Picture (Sunrise), dropped the following year (oscars.org 1929 page; English Wikipedia, "Category name changes").
findings.resolution: The card asks for Best Picture (listed as Outstanding Picture on oscars.org's 1929 page, whose highlights call Wings "The first Oscar winner for Best Picture") and a back note names Sunrise's separate award.

findings.issue: Wikidata's English label is "You Can't Take It With You"; oscars.org, the English Wikipedia and the Swedish article write "You Can't Take It with You". The Wikidata sv label is "Komedin om oss människor", with the alias "Komedien om oss människor"; the winner row of the Swedish list "Oscar för bästa film" (revision 59509021) also writes "Komedin om oss människor" (a link that redirects to the article); the Swedish article itself is titled "Komedien om oss människor", restored as the title in 2018 with the edit summary "ogjord rätt titel, tar bort den andra artikeln istället" (undone, right title, removing the other article instead).
